comments.rawMarkdown:
If anyone is interested in the results — they are quite weak. The only score of 0.17 was obtained after disabling almost the entire architecture. In practice, it was reduced to a simple chain: “minimal research → LLM hypothesis → verification and execution.”
All more complex versions — with memory, attempt limits, structured verification, and other components — failed at the stage of compatibility with the competition environment. Instead of refining the depth and sophistication of the agent’s logic, I spent all available time on the pure engineering task of making any agent run reliably in the official competition runtime.
Tomorrow I will submit the final version, but I have little hope for it.
My original goal was never to compete for a prize place. Given the timelines and my location in Russia, that would have been unrealistic. I participated primarily to test the ideas in practice.
Perhaps some engineers in the community will like the concepts and will be able to implement them more effectively in code.
In fact, I believe that a real AGI architecture can be built relatively quickly and does not require enormous compute resources. That said, even an RTX 6000 is clearly not enough. There is still a huge amount of work to be done — far more than one person, especially someone with my limited engineering background, can handle alone.

firstMessage.rawMarkdown:
This post is based on a paper I submitted to the ARC Prize Paper Track. At the time, I did not realize that Paper Track materials would remain private until the end of the competition. That is too long for me, so I am publishing the core idea here.

For a deeper ontological background, see [The Algorithm of Being](https://github.com/yakuninvladimir-ui/relational-information-research/blob/main/Philosophy/The%20Algorithm%20of%20Being%20Final.pdf). The architecture and specifications are available in the [Engineering section](https://github.com/yakuninvladimir-ui/relational-information-research/tree/main/Engineering).

There is also code on GitHub, but I want to be precise about my role. I am not a software engineer. I write code with ChatGPT Work, and even making an agent run correctly in the competition environment has taken substantial effort. I originally assumed that connecting the agent to the official sample would be mostly a matter of asking for the wrapper. It was not.

The present code should therefore be read as an experimental implementation, not as proof that the architecture has been fully realized. Perhaps someone in the competition will find the ideas useful and implement them more effectively.

## The problem is not only action selection

ARC-AGI-3 is interactive. An agent does not merely inspect a static grid and infer a transformation. It must act inside a changing environment whose local rules are initially unknown.

An available action may move an object, switch a mode, reveal a rule, produce no visible effect, or become meaningful only after another event. A visual change may be caused by the agent, by passive dynamics, or by an interaction that the agent has misunderstood.

The central problem is therefore not simply:

> Which action should be executed?

It is:

> What do the objects, actions, transitions, and goals mean in this particular environment, and when is that interpretation reliable enough to control action?

Human solvers bring a large semantic background to a short interaction trace. They recognize objects, tools, barriers, containment, symmetry, progress, completion, and game-like causality. A machine must either possess comparable priors or construct a task-local substitute from sparse evidence.

Pure search can collect transitions without knowing which distinctions matter. A semantic model can propose plausible interpretations without knowing which of them are true. The architecture must therefore separate **hypothesis**, **evidence**, and **authority to act**.

## Two central ideas

The first idea is **constraint**.

Information is treated not merely as stored data, but as restriction over a space of possibilities. An observation is useful when it excludes possible world models. An action is useful when its result either reduces uncertainty or advances a grounded objective.

The general sequence is:

```text
distinction -> constraint -> compression -> meaning -> model -> correction
```

Objects and relations are distinctions. Legal actions and observed transitions impose constraints. A compact world model compresses those constraints. Semantic reasoning proposes meaning. Verification corrects the model when the environment disagrees.

The second idea is **ternary logic with irrelevance**.

Binary verification is useful and necessary at the action boundary: an action may be legal or illegal, and a prediction may be satisfied or contradicted. Simpler agents can stop there.

But semantic reasoning requires a third outcome. A hypothesis may be neither supported nor contradicted because it is simply irrelevant to the current question or objective.

Following the distinction emphasized by Nikolay Brusentsov, irrelevance should not be confused with falsity. What is false must be excluded because it contradicts the active structure. What is irrelevant must be excluded because it does not participate in that structure.

In the operational form used here, a semantic hypothesis may be classified as:

* **required** — supported or necessary under the current constraints;
* **forbidden** — contradicted or incompatible with them;
* **irrelevant** — admissible in itself, but outside the active problem structure.

A separate state, **unresolved**, means that the evidence is still insufficient. It is not a fourth logical value.

This distinction matters because intelligence is not maximal exploration. It is disciplined narrowing. A system must learn not only what is true and false, but also what can be ignored.

## General architecture

The proposed architecture separates four epistemic functions.

### 1. World research

The agent converts official observations into stable objects, relations, action records, and before-and-after transitions.

Action identifiers have no universal meaning. Their semantics are inferred locally from evidence. The system asks bounded questions:

* What changed?
* What remained invariant?
* Which object or relation was affected?
* Was the change caused by the action or by passive dynamics?
* Did the available action surface itself change?

This layer records observations. It does not invent goals.

### 2. Semantic reasoning

A semantic module receives a compact structured description of the current world and proposes interpretations: possible object roles, action meanings, dynamics, goals, conditional plans, and observable milestones.

In the current competition-oriented design, a local language model is used for this role because semantic interpretation is part of the intelligence being tested. The point is not to let an LLM control the environment. The point is to place open-ended semantic reasoning inside an explicit system of constraints.

An LLM is not mandatory for every implementation of the general architecture. Another model or symbolic mechanism could perform the same role. But for AGI-oriented systems, some genuine semantic reasoning module is essential; otherwise the architecture reduces to a conventional binary controller with a verifier.

### 3. Grounding and operationalization

Semantic proposals are resolved against current object IDs, relation IDs, legal actions, and observed evidence.

Unsupported references are rejected rather than repaired by invention. A hypothesis becomes executable only when it can be reduced to a bounded test or plan with:

* identified targets;
* legal actions;
* predicted observable effects;
* explicit continuation or rejection conditions.

This is the boundary between meaning and operation.

### 4. Verification and control

Only the verifier may authorize an official action.

Before execution, it checks legality, grounding, previous evidence, expected effects, and repetition constraints. After execution, the official transition is used to update the hypothesis, the world model, and memory.

A predicted state is not a fact. A visible change is not automatically progress. A correct mechanical effect is not automatically evidence that the higher-level goal interpretation was correct.

The full loop is:

```text
observe -> structure -> research -> propose -> ground
-> verify -> act -> evaluate -> revise
```

The graph or object representation is a substrate for reasoning, not a source of goals. The semantic module is a source of hypotheses, not a controller. The verifier is a source of action authority, not semantic imagination.

## Irrelevance, memory, and recursive correction

Interactive reasoning cannot be represented adequately by success and failure alone.

A no-op may be useless, or it may answer a question about controllability. A legal action may work exactly as predicted but remain irrelevant to the current objective. A plausible hypothesis may fail in one semantic state and become worth reconsidering after the state changes.

For this reason, the agent should remember separately:

* contradicted or invalid hypotheses;
* irrelevant attempts;
* unresolved questions;
* observed action effects;
* verifier explanations;
* changes in object and relation identity.

The semantic module itself may be stateless. Recursion can be externalized through structured memory. Later semantic proposals receive the consequences of earlier actions, including why a route was rejected or ignored.

This makes self-correction auditable. The system should be able to state which official evidence changed a belief and why a previous route was abandoned.

## What is actually being claimed

The main contribution is not a new vision model, a new language model, or a finished ARC solver.

It is a control topology:

1. empirical world research before semantic commitment;
2. semantic hypothesis formation inside explicit constraints;
3. grounding before execution;
4. ternary separation of required, forbidden, and irrelevant;
5. independent verification at the action boundary;
6. structured memory for recursive correction.

The implementation evolved through several versions. Version 7.7 was broader and more complex. Version 8.3 deliberately removed much of that machinery and retained a compact verified hypothesis loop. Version 9 continues the experiment, but it should not be treated as a complete or authoritative realization of the architecture.

The falsifiable claim is simpler:

* actions should be traceable to grounded hypotheses;
* imagined states must not become official facts;
* visible change must not automatically confirm meaning;
* irrelevant routes should be remembered without becoming universal prohibitions;
* every semantic commitment must remain revisable by official evidence.

ARC-AGI-3 is not only a search problem. It is a problem of constructing meaning under sparse interaction without allowing imagined meaning to become uncontrolled action.

The proposed answer is **constraint before control**.

**Vladimir Yakunin, 2026**
